what_happened: The person running Athena saw that six fixes the steward queued the night before sit at places 364 to 374 of a 203-item plan. They include read-only filters for producers, showing policy denials to the error review, stopping unreadable background commands, retrying the shared build folder with its goal unchanged, fixing study claim c45, and running clippy before verification. At about 20 dispatches a day they would not run for weeks, while stale late-October requests run first. The one-in-three improvement turn reaches only a few older Athena items. The person running Athena did not reorder the queue by hand. They reported it for the steward and the planner.
cause: Queue order is set by age and tier, not by value. Nothing retires stale or duplicate items, and nothing weighs a fix for a known failure class above ordinary requests. Athena's own corrective fixes therefore wait in line behind a backlog that keeps growing, and what it learns is not acted on. The improvement turn is a fixed share of dispatches, with no link to how many fixes are waiting.
prevention: Give Athena-originated fix items for recorded failure classes their own lane. Dispatch from that lane ahead of ordinary requests, within a share cap so it cannot starve the owner's work. Add a standing backlog review that retires or revalidates requests older than a set age, so the queue stays short enough for order to matter. Have the plan show each item's wait time. Warn when a steward-queued fix is placed beyond a set number of days of dispatch capacity.
proposed_request: Make the queue dispatch fixes for recorded failure classes ahead of ordinary requests. Outcome: items that the steward or the failure review queues to fix a recorded failure class run before older ordinary items. They use a reserved lane with a cap of at most half of daily dispatches, so owner-filed requests are not starved. The plan and status page show each item's lane and expected days to dispatch. Athena flags any fix item whose expected wait is over 2 days. Add a standing review that lists ordinary requests older than 14 days and proposes retiring, revalidating or keeping each; it closes nothing without a recorded reason. Acceptance: (1) a test with a queue of 200 older ordinary items and 6 new fix items dispatches all 6 fix items within the first 12 dispatches, with ordinary items still dispatched in the remainder; (2) the plan output shows lane and expected wait; (3) the stale-request review runs on a cadence with no manual command and records its proposals. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
